title: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748, 119th Congress) - statutory platform safeguards for minors

business_activity.name: Family of Apps social platforms used by under-17s

authority: US Senate (Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee)
policy_mechanism: Statute: mandatory tools and safeguards on covered online platforms for users under 17, enforced as a product-design obligation

mechanism_chain.text: S.1748 would require covered online platforms, including social media platforms, to implement tools and safeguards to protect users under 17.
The Senate Commerce Committee ordered the bill reported favorably with an amendment on August 5, 2026 - committee-stage activity, not enacted law.

If enacted, safeguards and duty-of-care style obligations would land on Instagram and Facebook product design for minors; Meta already discloses state laws restricting services to minors, showing the mechanism family is active at multiple levels of government.

events.description: S.1748 introduced and referred to Senate Commerce
Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably
Meta FY2025 10-K discloses state laws restricting services to minors and legislation limiting advertising to minors

financial_linkage.detail: No under-17 revenue or engagement breakdown is disclosed; consolidated FY2025 revenue $201.0B (XBRL) is not allocatable to this cohort.
financial_linkage.gap: Product-level exposure for minors is Unknown per the financial linkage ladder.

rationale: Emerging list, Proposal status: a favorably reported committee bill is legislative activity, not adoption - the proposal trap applies. Business exposure is Meaningful because the affected cohort is bounded but the obligations would touch core product surfaces. Confidence High on the process facts (Tier A legislative record); the business-effect chain remains inferred.
